Prevention: Establish plantations far away from unattended cashew trees
Ensure cashew trees are well- spaced in new plots.
On pure stands it is 12mx12m; when intercropped with crops like pigeon peas it is 18mx12m.
Prune to provide good ventilation within trees, making microclimate less suitable for disease
Kingowe cutters or hands to prune off-season shoots and flowers which are sources of mildew
Monitoring: Visit field once per week after harvest (November for
Coastal areas) and when newly unwanted off- season plant parts have developed (during onset of the heavy rain season- masika)
Search for fine dusty-white to grey powder - mycelia on surface of tender tissues - shoots, leaves, flowers or panicle and fruits).
If 1 tree is infested out of 5 to 6 trees then consider action.
Direct Control: Prune after harvest to remove suckers which create favourable conditions for mildew.
Remove off- season cashew nut fruits since they are breeding areas for powdery mildew
Dust cashew trees with sulphur –based products (e.g.Sulphur, Kumulus, Sulgro, ThiovitJet, Salfa, and others).
Usually 0.25kg/tree or 9kg/acre/ season but always double- check the product label.
Bayfidan 250EC, Agromenol 250EC, Defender 250EC, Falmenol 250EC, Mupafidan 250EC, and many others).
Usually applied at 0.7 – 1l /20 litre of water/acre but double- check the product label.
Restrictions: Wear protective clothing that is gloves, a mask, boots, overall, hat, goggles.
Always consult recent list of registered pesticides (MAFC / TPRI).
III (slightly hazardous); multi-side action pesticides; pre-harvest interval p.h.i. 7 days; restricted re-entry interval 1 day after spray.
Max 4 sprays with minimal 14 d interval.
Apply at an interval of 14 days for the 1st three applications.
If powdery mildew still spreads, the 4th dust application is to be done at an interval of 21 days.
At that time there is dew for sulphur dust to stick on leaves.
Ensure thorough coverage; dust whole tree.
Max 1 spray, p.h.i. 30-35 days, r.e.i. 3 days.
